steps.why: Framed on the three marks rather than pinned to the end. A messenger critic measured two of the eleven capabilities this artifact is supposed to enumerate — editing and taking a message back — visible in no artifact at all: the report named an edited row and the still's first drawn sheet began 84 px below where that row ended, so it was just off the top. `end` frames the newest note and the staging writes four more rows after the edit. This asks for the tightest stretch that holds an edited row, a row taken back and one still in the outbox, and the framing machinery measures what actually lands on the glass and keeps the best it finds.
